title: What people live by
hookLine: in Tolstoy's story an angel learns that people live by love (What Men Live By)

cards: Winter, in a Russian village. A poor shoemaker named Simon is walking home with no sheepskin, because the people who owed him money didn't pay.
Behind a roadside shrine he sees something pale: a man, naked, sitting against the wall, freezing. Simon is frightened. He walks right past.
Then, a little way down the road, he stops, argues with himself, and turns back. That turn begins a short story by Leo Tolstoy called What Men Live By.

teach.b: Simon gives the man his coat and brings him home. His wife Matryona is furious: no sheepskin, and now another mouth to feed. Then she looks at the stranger, and pity wins.
She sets out bread, and the stranger, for the first time, smiles. He gives his name as Michael, and stays on, learning to make shoes.

teach.h: BOOTS FOR A YEAR, SLIPPERS FOR A BODY.
teach.b: One day a wealthy gentleman storms in and orders boots that must last a year without losing their shape. As he gives the order, Michael looks past him and smiles a second time. Then Michael makes soft slippers instead.
Simon is horrified, until a servant runs back: the master has died on the way home, and they need slippers for the body.

teach.h: TWIN GIRLS, RAISED BY A NEIGHBOR.
teach.b: Later a woman comes in with twin girls, one of them lame. Their mother died when they were born, and this neighbor took them in and raised them as her own. Michael smiles a third time.
Then he reveals that he is an angel.
He was sent to take the twins' mother's soul and refused out of pity, so he was sent to earth to learn three things.
What dwells in people: love. What isn't given to people: to know their own needs, even what they'll need by evening. And what people live by.
Not by careful planning for themselves, the angel says, but by love.

how: Tolstoy's short story What Men Live By is a moral tale; readers take from it the angel's three answers: love dwells in people, no one knows their own needs, and people live by love.

o: the rich man who orders boots to last a year
the poor shoemaker who turns back in the snow
the stranger, an angel, who learns what people live by

games.q: who's who in the story — tap the pairs.
p: the poor shoemaker who turns back
the stranger who smiles three times
raised the twins as her own

s: Simon helps the stranger the moment he sees him
he's frightened and walks past, then stops and turns back.
the rich man needed slippers for his body, not boots
he died on the way home, and Michael had already made slippers.

games.q: you're Simon, walking home in winter. behind the shrine, a naked man is freezing. what do you do?
o: walk past, then stop and turn back.
games.why: in the story, Simon does both: he's frightened and walks past, then argues with himself and turns back. the whole story begins with that turn.

practice: The twins lived because someone who didn't have to took them in; look back over your own life the same way. Who fed you, taught you, drove you, sat up with you when you were sick?
Let the names and faces come one at a time, family and maybe a surprise or two, a teacher, a neighbor, a stranger at the right moment, and if you pray, give thanks in your own tradition's words.

wordCard.voice: Michael. The angel in Tolstoy's story who learns, through a shoemaker's family, that people live not by planning but by love. Today's word.

carryVoice: Your line: what we live by. Three smiles, three answers. Day eight hundred fifty-five, done.

sources.ref: Leo Tolstoy, What Men Live By
